method: headless Chrome DOM + geometry + persisted-state mirror + canvas pixel census only; no vision. Screenshots are hashed mirrors, not inspected visually. Selection driven by real canvas taps (App.applyGestureOutput -> pickTarget -> setSelected); every mutation through panel buttons/selects -> props.dispatch -> applyCommand. Form factors: phone 390x844 dpr2 portrait, phoneland 844x390 dpr2 rail, desktop 1920x1080 dpr1 rail; all five scenario loops run on each.

fixtureScrutiny.a: Only setup seeding mutates state: fixtures derived from docs/evidence/yard-mature.json before encoding with the game's own encodeSave arithmetic (FNV-1a checksum, lastSeenMs=Date.now()). partial removes route 1, raises store scrap to 60 and parks every drone (repaired=false) to stop scrap INCOME during the flow; the freshly laid belt itself still transports scrap, so the refund checks verify the preview price/refund against the engine's beltCost/refundOf identities rather than an isolated store delta. missingInput removes route 4. zeroPower and outputFull are ENGINE-DRIVEN, not hand-set statuses: zeroPower keeps every machine mid-batch (progress=1, batchMilli=1e9) and raises the sorter batchPower to 2000 so the engine's allocatePower yields ratio 8/2015 (~0%) and startBatches marks all powerLimited; outputFull fills the sorter tray to its outputBuffer (12) and saturates its output belts so enqueueCargo keeps the tray full and the engine sets outputFull. All set reducedMotion=true for stable pixels. No src changes; every action is a real UI tap/click through dispatch -> applyCommand.
fixtureScrutiny.b: Documented in this probe header, the derive* functions and results.json.
fixtureScrutiny.c: Seeded envelopes pass the game's full decodeSave/repairRegistration/validateSim; the 00-open steps assert the loaded mirror matches the seed. Route references pruned exactly like repairRegistration. No invariant weakened or bypassed.
fixtureScrutiny.d: No action faked by injection; localStorage read only as the game's own persistence mirror (written on every ok dispatch). The refund scenario connects a fresh belt through the real UI (engine prices its run) then disconnects it, because mature belts are pre-price (run:null, refund 0).

pixelCensus.orange: r>g+25 && g>=b && r>120 (blocked rail; residue cargo shares the hue, so blocked is corroborated by DOM route status)
pixelCensus.railBand: g>r+40 && b>r+50 && b>=120 && b<=185 && g<=175 (working-rail-over-floor ink; excludes full-cyan pips b232, body grays and dimmed rails b<120)
pixelCensus.visibilityClaim: strictly relative: visible.cyan > hidden.cyan, hidden.cyan < 0.5*visible.cyan, and the rail-band set diff (railRemoved) >= 10 pixels both when hiding (ink removed) and showing (ink restored); route count unchanged while hidden.

findings.detail: The yard-wide production/power overview and bottleneck list live inside the machine inspector's Bottleneck section, and the route legend + visibility toggle inside its Transport section. A dedicated always-on dock would require editing App.tsx/Hud.tsx, which #62 owns and #59 forbids. The surfaces are reachable the real way (tap any machine) and derive every number from state.

Each bottleneck's Show route focuses a belt touching the affected machine on the canvas through the shared view bridge (a real, visible repaint). Swapping the inspected machine to the bottleneck's machine is not offered because App.tsx exposes no selection callback and is owned by #62; the overview tells the player to open the machine from the yard instead.

The simulation has no in-place filter-edit command, so the controls state this plainly and offer disconnect + re-lay rather than a disabled fake control. Connect/disconnect/filter-at-lay are the real supported capabilities, each with a cost/validity preview and Cancel.
